core_principles: Changing hand formation from a supinated to a neutral grip alters the biomechanics of the arm during elbow flexion.
There is no significant difference in brachioradialis muscle activity, torque, or power during the initial 0-40 degrees of elbow flexion between a neutral and a supinated grip.
The brachioradialis acts primarily as a synergist muscle during both neutral and supinated elbow flexion under heavy loads.
A pronated (overhand) grip places the biceps brachii at a biomechanical disadvantage, which significantly increases the activation of the brachioradialis to perform elbow flexion.

Both neutral and supinated grips keep the biceps brachii in an optimal position to perform elbow flexion efficiently, meaning the brachioradialis does not have to activate as much compared to a pronated grip.
common_mistakes: Using a pronated grip when the primary goal is to target the biceps brachii, which places the biceps brachii at a biomechanical disadvantage.
specific_findings: Study population: 5 male participants (Age 23.6 ± 1.1 yrs, Height 178.2 ± 5.9 cm, Weight 79.8 ± 10.4 kg).
The mean value of average torque during the initial 40 degrees of elbow flexion during a neutral grip was 34.22 ± 6.14 N*m and 33.84 ± 7.56 N*m during a supinated bicep curl (p>.05).
The mean value for power during the initial 40 degrees of elbow flexion during a neutral grip bicep curl was 49.35 ± 8.61 watts and 53.04 ± 14.70 watts during a supinated bicep curl.

core_principles: Neutral grip and supinated grip bicep curls show similar brachioradialis muscle activity and performance during the initial 40 degrees of elbow flexion.
The choice between a neutral grip and a supinated grip does not significantly alter the torque or power output during the start of the lift.
specific_findings: The mean value for power during the initial 40 degrees of elbow flexion during a neutral grip bicep curl was 49.35 ± 8.61 watts and 53.04 ± 14.70 watts during a supinated bicep curl (p > .05).
The mean value for MVC% for the brachioradialis during the first 40 degrees was 67.70 ± 9.08% during a neutral grip bicep curl and 63.84 ± 8.19% during a supinated bicep curl.
The mean value for the average EMG activity for the brachioradialis during a neutral grip bicep curl was 565.17 ± 163.80 μvolts and 541.80 ± 165.46 μvolts during a supinated bicep curl (p = .051).
The mean value for average torque during the first 40° of a neutral grip bicep curl was 34.22 ± 6.14 N*m and 33.84 ± 7.56 N*m during a supinated grip bicep curl (p > .05).
